newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power dips before cool weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power dips before cool weekend.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. dipped Fridayahead of forecasts of a cool weekend for the region, market sources said.
"It seems like a cold front is pushing through," said one Southeast-based power marketer.

In the Southeastern Reliability Council (SERC), non-firm power for heavy demand hours over the weekend was quoted at $14.00-$16.00 for delivery into the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory, compared with Thursday's $15.00-$16.00. Monday's peak electricity at northern TVA was assessed near $16.50.
Peak power at southern TVA for the weekend was valued in the $15.00-$16.00 range off from Thursday's $16.00-$17.00, and for Monday $17.50-$18.00.
Off-peak, weekend electricity into TVA was pegged at $11.00-$12.50.
At the Georgia/Florida border, peak, non-firm electricity was quoted near $19.25 a MWh for Saturday; $18.25 for Sunday; and $20.00-$20.50 for Monday.
Thursday's quote for Friday peak power at the Ga./Fla. border was $19.50-$20.50.
Florida Power Corp's 825 MW Crystal River 3 nuclear unit in Red Level. Fla., remained shut following repairs to a leaky section of line that feeds lubrication oil to the unit's turbine shaft.
